_shell_revision_comment: The revision of agents/SHELL.md this surface was built against. SHELL.md's own revision block asks for it, and the reason is good: every lane so far has found a defect in that document, and a surface that records which revision it was built against is the only way to know later which pages carry a fix and which predate it. r4 = tier-4 band variant, --fg3 at .55, §8 identifying animation required. NOTE: the revision block was added to SHELL.md while this lane was running; the document read at the start of the run already contained all of r2, r3 and r4, so this surface is r4 in substance as well as in label.
_nav_tier_comment: ampersand-nav/src/amp-nav.js (HEAD d0a6415) records `deliberatic: { place: 3, rung: "spec", spec: "…docs.ampersandboxdesign.com…" }`. Place 3 is "a specification in the ComputeDriven world" — NOT the place-2 layer sentence, and NOT the place-4 attribution variant. SHELL.md §1 says check the tier before you write the band, because that is exactly how gpscoord shipped a membership claim its own nav excluded. Checked 2026-08-16.
question: Can disagreement be preserved and governed rather than averaged away?
_gate_divergence_comment: 2026-08-17. This surface's launch gate no longer measures its identifying decoration with a single byte cap over the whole source file. That single cap is still what agentromatic, fleetprompt and specprompt use, so this gate and those three now differ, deliberately; delegatic took the same split the same day. The reason is written where the checks are: the shared cap counted explanatory prose against a budget whose stated subject is what runs on a handset, and this surface's decoration carries a great deal of prose because SHELL.md asks every lane to write down what it learned. The gate now bounds the executable part and the download separately, and both were broken on purpose and seen to refuse before this line was written.
surface_rung_covers: the protocol document at docs/spec/README.md, v0.1-draft — no line of Deliberatic has been written and nothing on this domain runs
_rung_witness_comment: Which gate establishes the surface rung. launch-gate.mjs refuses if THAT gate is not approved. GPSCoord's rule — 'any pending gate keeps the surface below live_deployed' — is too blunt: independent_use is pending forever by construction, so under that rule no surface could ever reach a deployed rung.

type_metrics._comment: SHELL.md r7. A line box smaller than the display face's own box makes consecutive lines' em boxes overlap and a descender reads as clipped — Travis reported it as the g of 'agents' being cut off on agentromatic. MEASURED, not assumed: each element's text was rendered to a canvas in its own computed font and canvas measureText's fontBoundingBoxAscent+Descent (the face's own box) and actualBoundingBoxAscent+Descent (this string's ink) were compared against the line box, at viewport widths 390 and 1280, against the served page. BOTH bounds matter and each of the three governance sites was worst on a different one: Syne overflowed its font box by 12.09 px while its ink fitted with 7.91 px to spare; Newsreader's font box fitted and its INK cleared by 0.91 px. required_ratio is max(font_box_ratio, ink_box_ratio) + 0.04; the margin absorbs the +-1 px integer quantisation of fontBoundingBox (Syne at 20 px reports 25, which is 1.25 rather than its 1.2043) and leaves visible clearance. launch-gate reads line-height back out of the EMITTED stylesheet and refuses below required_ratio. These numbers belong to this face at these weights; another surface must re-measure rather than copy them.
type_metrics.measured_with: agent-browser --session triofix (Chrome), canvas measureText in each element's own computed font, viewport widths 390 and 1280, against the served page

status.statement: A specification, and this page. The weighted bipolar argumentation framework, the two-phase consensus, the constitution DSL, the Merkle evidence chains and the reputation system are all written down in detail, and none of them have been implemented.
status.source: docs/spec/README.md in this repository, v0.1-draft. Every section number cited on this page was checked to resolve in it on 2026-08-16.
status.limit: This establishes that a document exists and that it addresses the dimensions named below. It does not establish that the semantics converge on any real graph, that the consensus protocol is correct, or that a single line of Deliberatic has ever run. A specification that covers a gap and a system that closes it are different objects.

advance.requires: Code in a repository that implements §2.2 graded semantics and passes a test. The transport bindings in §7 are specified for A2A, MCP and raw HTTP, so an implementation that is not ours would move this further still — that is the only thing that can.

citation.title: Governance Gaps in Agent Interoperability Protocols: What MCP, A2A, and ACP Cannot Express
citation._peer_reviewed_comment: It is a preprint. The page says so in --warn, and the paper's own 'Partial classification involves judgment' limitation is quoted rather than hidden. A source cited only where it flatters is not a source.
citation.scoring: 2 points for Supported, 1 for Partial, 0 for Absent, over six dimensions — 12 possible.

retraction_blocklist._comment: SHELL.md r6, hole 1. The old check asked 'is the retraction present?' and stopped, so a page could KEEP its retraction and reinstate the retracted sentence anywhere else and still pass — a real deliberate break did exactly that. Presence is not the property; CONFINEMENT is. Every needle below is counted in the raw artifact AND in the r8-correct extracted text, and every occurrence must fall inside the retraction region. `max_total` bounds the count so the retraction cannot be padded with reinstated copies of what it retracts. Counts are the ones measured at the commit that introduced this field; a needle whose count changes is a page whose retraction changed, and the gate refuses either way.

terms.why: The retracted control. Twice inside the retraction — 'A waitlist button' and 'no waitlist to join' — and nowhere else. This is the needle that shows why a bound is needed rather than a boolean.
The promise the old control made about a list that did not exist. Once.
The label the old button gave itself without achieving anything. Once.
The charge against the old control. Once.

contact._comment: SHELL.md r9, ruled by Travis 2026-08-17. Contact is the ComputeDriven Formspree form and `form_endpoint` is where it posts — the same endpoint computedriven.com uses. This closes the [TRAVIS] item fourteen surfaces were blocked on; until today this record said 'no Formspree endpoint exists for this domain and borrowing another's needs a ruling', and corrections went to GitHub issues. `url` is kept as the SECOND route, not the first, and `kind` stays not-mailto: this page carried mailto:hello@ampersandboxdesign.com until 2026-08-16 and the gate still refuses one anywhere in the artifact. The form is a real <form action method=POST>, so it delivers with JavaScript off; src/say.js only upgrades it to an inline reply and prints success solely on a 2xx.
